A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiZOO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model fine-tuning results, synthetic optimization experiments, ablations and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Phi-2/Llama3 evaluations, HiZOO-L comparisons and measured per-step timings.

M1.justification: v2 introduces HiZOO-L, which stores row/column factors of curvature information and reconstructs preconditioners for perturbations and updates (Appendix D.2, Algorithm 3). This substantially extends v1's diagonal-state method. HiZOO-multi largely corresponds to v1's existing multisample variant, although its pseudocode now includes the preconditioning factor in projected gradients.

E1.justification: The NLP datasets, task requirements and three synthetic test functions are retained. Phi-2 and Llama3 introduce model configurations on existing tasks. The missing many-shot RoBERTa table changes result reporting, rather than establishing different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The predictive baseline families are largely retained, with some LoRA/prefix results aggregated as PEFT. However, the memory comparison removes the prefix-FT comparator present in v1 Tables 5 and 9; it is absent from v2 Figure 6 and Table 10.

E3.justification: v2 adds Phi-2 (2.7B), Llama3 (8B), controlled A100 timing measurements and forward-pass-based efficiency comparisons. Toy convergence comparisons explicitly use a loss threshold of 0.1. Table 4 now labels objectives as F1, whereas v1's caption specified classification accuracy; unchanged scores do not establish reruns. Existing RoBERTa/OPT hyperparameter grids and training budgets remain.

E4.justification: New comparisons test whether curvature compression preserves accuracy and convergence, using HiZOO-L versus HiZOO on OPT-13B and Llama3 (Table 5, Figures 12–14), alongside additional efficiency analysis. The SNLI smoothing-scale sweep expands to include 1, 1e-2 and 1e-4. Existing multisampling and Hessian-term-omission ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The retained RoBERTa accuracy table still reports means and standard deviations across five runs. No additional training-run counts, seed studies, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced. The new timing average over 100 steps specifies measurement sampling, rather than independent training repetitions or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds model, HiZOO-L and timing results, while removing v1's many-shot RoBERTa Table 7 and separate few-shot PEFT rows. Retained OPT scores also change: HiZOO's OPT-13B MultiRC result changes from 55.5 to 61.3 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 8). OPT-30B MeZO-prefix RTE changes from 72.6 to 66.1, reversing its ranking against HiZOO's unchanged 68.6 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 9).

T1.justification: The Hessian smoothing recursion changes from updating Sigma to updating Sigma inverse (v1 Equation 4; v2 Equation 6), a substantive mathematical correction. Smoothness and convergence statements are also rewritten using minibatch losses. The principal proof structure, Gaussian-moment lemma and O(epsilon^-4) convergence rate remain.

C1.justification: The contribution set expands to include HiZOO-L and preservation of predictive performance with memory close to MeZO. The highlighted SST-2 claim changes from up to 30-fold step reduction to an eightfold forward-pass speedup and reported 1.55% accuracy improvement averaged across models. The original novelty claim about Hessian-informed zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets HiZOO-L's similar performance as suggesting noise in the Hessian estimates and motivates further compression (Appendix D.2). It also uses measured per-step costs to justify forward-pass counts as a runtime proxy. The memory limitation receives more explicit treatment, while v1's general recommendation of smoothing scale 1e-6 is removed.

D1.justification: The code-access URL and existing hyperparameter grids remain unchanged. v2 adds low-rank implementation pseudocode and timing details covering 80GB A100 hardware, lack of NV-Link, batch sizes and measurement length. Some earlier disclosures disappear, including Table 4's explicit classification sample count and task-specific tuning configurations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Adafactor as motivation for HiZOO-L, plus citations concerning QLoRA, GaLore, LISA, FlashAttention and Phi models. The optimizer literature review and central positioning relative to MeZO remain largely unchanged. These citations do not establish additional evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution list are rewritten, the update procedure precedes the Hessian estimator, convergence analysis moves into Methods, and toy visualization moves before the LLM experiments. Appendices are reorganized around test functions, variants, consolidated model experiments and timing. The generic impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 adds an optimizer schematic, benchmark bars, compression plots and a timing table; existing tables gain averages or combine PEFT rows. Numerous loss plots use forward-pass axes, toy results are redistributed between main text and appendix, and the many-shot and hardware-capacity tables disappear.

improvement.justification: HiZOO-L addresses a concrete weakness: v2 Table 10 reports 29GB versus 53GB for standard HiZOO on OPT-13B, with similar accuracy in Table 5. Measured timings and additional model evaluations strengthen the practical evidence. These gains are tempered by missing many-shot and separate PEFT results and new reporting errors: for example, Table 1 lists an FT average of 74.9 although its entries average 73.05. The net improvement is therefore limited.
